items.title: lease acquire --wait SECONDS
items.action: Copy the planned test file from docs/plans/2023/tests/tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_lease_wait.py to tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_lease_wait.py first. In locking.py change acquire to `acquire(cfg: HarnessConfig, owner: str, wait: Optional[float] = None) -> str` and pass `wait` on: `catalog_lock.acquire_lease(lock_path(cfg), owner, wait)`; its docstring says it waits up to `wait` seconds for a held lease or write lock (catalog_lock.WAIT_SECONDS when None). `leased` keeps calling `acquire(cfg, owner)`. In todo_sync.py add a module-level argparse type `_seconds(text: str) -> float` (float(text); a non-number or a negative value raises argparse.ArgumentTypeError('must be a number of seconds, 0 or more'), so argparse reports `argument --wait: ...`). In `_leases` add `acq.add_argument("--wait", type=_seconds, metavar="SECONDS", help="Wait up to SECONDS for a held lease or write lock before refusing (default: 10).")` after --owner; `_lease`'s acquire branch calls `locking.acquire(cfg, args.owner, args.wait)`. Module docstring: the entry reads ``lease acquire --owner TEXT [--wait SECONDS]`` and adds that --wait sets how long a held lease or write lock is waited on before the refusal (default 10 seconds; a todo-editor split passes 300). todo_sync.md: in `lease acquire` add the row `| `--wait SECONDS` | Wait up to SECONDS for a held lease or write lock before refusing (default 10). A todo-editor split passes 300. |` after --owner, and in Locking add that `lease acquire --wait SECONDS` waits that long instead of 10 seconds. items.title: Split drafts its spec before it takes the lease
items.action: Copy docs/plans/2023/tests/tests/skills/test_todo_editor_split_lease_contract.py to tests/skills/test_todo_editor_split_lease_contract.py first. In todo-editor.md renumber the split section: 1. read the item and what it points at, find the independent deliverables (old step 2); a one-deliverable item stops and reports that, and no lease is held yet, so no release runs (drop '(the **finish** release still runs)'). 2. write the spec to `<state_dir>/todo-sync/split-<id>.json` (old step 3, unchanged; the path is per id, so parallel drafts never collide). 3. `TS lease acquire --owner "todo-editor split" --wait 300`, run with a Bash timeout of 330000 ms; keep the token; every split command below passes `--lease <token>`. A `problem:` line naming a holder means another run holds the catalog: run the same command again, up to 3 times in all; the third refusal ends the run (relay it); any other `problem:` line ends the run at once. 4. the dry run (old step 4), adding that it reads the catalog as it is now, so a split that landed while this one drafted shows up here as a `problem:` line: fix the spec and rerun once. 5-7: old steps 5-7. Rules, 'Queue, never write': keep the sync/add sentence; replace the lease sentence with: Retire and refresh hold the catalog lease from their first step to their reply; a split drafts its spec first and holds the lease from the step before its dry run to its reply, so several splits draft at once and apply one at a time; either way no drain or other run writes in between. finish: 'Runs for retire, split and refresh once they hold a lease.' Stop conditions: add that a split stopping before its lease step holds none and runs no release. In tests/skills/test_todo_inbox_prose_contract.py change only the module docstring sentence 'Retire, split and refresh runs hold a lease from start to reply.' to 'Retire and refresh runs hold a lease from start to reply, a split from its dry run to its reply.'

items.title: Field updates: validate, queue and drain
items.action: Copy docs/plans/2023/tests/tests/lib/test_todo_sync_updates.py to tests/lib/test_todo_sync_updates.py first. reshape.py: `_check_types(n, spec, label: str = "item")` and `_check_item(n, item, label: str = "item")` put `label` where they now say `item` in their messages (callers unchanged); read_spec names the spec from {"parts": "split spec", "items": "add spec", "updates": "update spec"}. New updates.py (module docstring; functions under 50 lines): `UPDATE_FIELDS` = the ADD_REQUIRED + ADD_OPTIONAL keys less ISSUE_KEYS, in that order; frozen dataclass `Updated(catalog, updated, rescored, reranked)` where `updated` is a tuple of (id, fields tuple), one entry per item in first-update order, its fields merged in first-set order; `merge_updated(pairs)` does that merge and the drain reuses it. `apply_updates(catalog, entries) -> Updated` works on a deep copy: todo_ids.require_stable(catalog, "update"); an empty list raises 'update needs at least one update in the spec'; per entry n (from 1): not a dict -> 'update n is not an object'; no non-empty string `id` -> 'update n names no id'; `fields` missing, not a dict or empty -> 'update n sets no field'; a key outside UPDATE_FIELDS -> 'update n sets <key>; an update never sets it'; reshape._check_types(n, fields, "update"); the id through todo_ids.resolve_ids (a retired, split or unknown id raises its message, prefixed 'update n: '); an (id, field) an earlier entry of the same list set -> 'update n sets <id> <field> again; one spec sets a field once'; then the item takes a deep copy of each value and reshape._check_item(n, item, "update") runs; finally reshape._rerank(data) and the Updated. inbox.py: `_write_items(cfg, items, key: str = "items")` writes `{key: [item]}`; new `put_updates(cfg, spec) -> PutResult`: read_spec(spec, "updates"), load_catalog(cfg, "update"), apply_updates (RankingError becomes TodoSyncError; nothing written on any refusal), then _write_items(cfg, entries, "updates"). The drain reads each claimed file as updates when its object holds an "updates" list, else as add items as now; an update file runs apply_updates on the working catalog, a (id, field) an earlier file of the same drain set is appended once to `overwritten`, and any TodoSyncError, RankingError or ValueError rejects the file as an add file is rejected. Keep _absorb under 50 lines (a per-file helper). DrainResult gains `updated` and `overwritten` (both default ()), after `drift`; drain passes them by keyword. A drain where only updates landed still writes, renders and checks. The failure text after a landing names what landed: 'inbox: added ..., then:' or 'inbox: updated ..., then:' or both joined by '; '. drain_lines: nothing landed and nothing refused -> 'inbox: empty'; nothing landed -> 'inbox: rejected K (<names>)' as now; else 'inbox: ' + '; '.join of, in order, 'added N item(s): <id> (#N|note), ...', 'updated M item(s): <id> (<f1>, <f2>), ...', 'overwrote <id> <field>, ...', 'rejected K (<names>)', then 'check drift=D' (the formats[] example). Update the inbox.py module docstring: the inbox also holds field updates, one per file, applied by the same drain.

items.title: inbox put --update in the driver and its usage document
items.action: Copy docs/plans/2023/tests/tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_update_cli.py to tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_update_cli.py first. todo_sync.py `_adders`: on `put` add `--update` (store_true, help 'Queue field updates of existing items: the spec is {"updates": [{"id": ..., "fields": {...}}]}.'). `_inbox`: with args.update, a --file-issue raises TodoSyncError('inbox put --update takes no --file-issue (an update files no issue)'), else `inbox.put_updates(cfg, args.spec)`; either way print one `queued <repo-relative path>` line per file as now. Module docstring: the entry reads ``inbox put --spec PATH [--file-issue | --update]`` and says --update queues field updates of existing items (each field one an add spec may carry other than issue and url; each id a live item, a retired or split id refused; one spec sets a field of an item once; the whole spec checked against the catalog first, then one inbox file per update); the ``add`` entry's --inbox sentence says queued updates are applied with the queued items in name order, then the catalog is re-ranked, a later queued update of a field an earlier one set wins and the line names it, and gives the line as `inbox: [added N item(s): ...; ][updated M item(s): <id> (<fields>), ...; ][overwrote <id> <field>, ...; ][rejected K (<files>); ]check drift=D`. Update the first paragraph's list to name field updates. todo_sync.md: Who runs what, `inbox put` row: the todo-editor for add and sync runs, and with --update for update runs (any agent may queue updates); `add --inbox` row: '/harness:add-todo, /harness:sync-gh-todo and /harness:todo-edit --update after their agents return, and the todo-watch mod'; `add` table, --inbox row: names the applied updates and the line above; `inbox put` section: a paragraph on --update and a `| `--update` | ... |` row.

items.title: todo-edit: parallel splits and the update operation
items.action: Copy docs/plans/2023/tests/tests/skills/test_todo_edit_parallel_contract.py to tests/skills/test_todo_edit_parallel_contract.py first. todo-edit SKILL.md: argument-hint "--retire ID[, ID ...] [--delete-retired] | --split ID[, ID ...] | --update ID[, ID ...] | --refresh  [-- <guidance>]"; description adds queuing field updates of items (trigger 'update todo-m3x9'). Step 1 table: `--split` one or more (`--split todo-m3x9, k7qf -- one part per module`, opus); new row `--update` one or more, guidance required (`--update todo-m3x9 -- severity 4: the parser drops rows`, opus). Stop conditions: drop '`--split` names more than one id'; add '`--update` with no guidance' and '`--update` names none' to the hint cases. Step 2: `--retire` and `--refresh` make one Agent call as now; `--split` and `--update` make one `Agent` call per id, all in one message, each prompt naming its one id on the `Ids:` line (splits then draft at once and take the catalog lease one at a time; updates only queue). The prompt block keeps its six lines with `Operation: <retire | split | refresh | update>`. New Step 3, for --update only: once every agent has returned, drain once with a fenced line `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hpy" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/todo_sync.py" add --inbox` run from the project root, reading its line as add-todo Step 4 does (`inbox: updated ...`, `; rejected ...` naming files kept as `.rejected.json` beside a `.reason.txt`, `inbox: empty` when nothing waited or the todo-watch mod drained first, a lock held by `todo_sync.py add --inbox` meaning the mod is draining). Old Step 3 becomes Step 4: relay every agent's reply, one per id, then the drain line. todo-editor.md: frontmatter description adds queuing field updates of existing items and the update operation; Rules 'Edit only' adds update spec files; 'Queue, never write' covers sync, add and update; new `## update` section after `## add`: Runs for `Operation: update`, `Ids:` one item, `Guidance:` what to change. 1. Grep and Read the item; read what the guidance names, checking claims as add level 1 does. 2. Choose new values only for `title`, `kind`, `status`, `needs_decision`, `decision_question`, `summary`, `proposed_change`, `code_snippet`, `files`, `blast_radius`, `loe`, `impact`, `severity`, `why_ranked`, `related_gh_issues`; each value replaces the field whole; the script refuses every other field (`id`, `rank`, `priority`, `depends_on`, `unblocks`, `sources`, `gh_issues`, `tracker`, `catalog_entry_ids`), and the drain rescores from severity, impact, loe and blast_radius. 3. Write `{"updates": [{"id": "<id>", "fields": {...}}]}` to `<state_dir>/todo-sync/update-<stamp>-<rand>.json` (stamp and rand as in sync). 4. `TS inbox put --update --spec <path>`: no lease, no catalog write; on a `problem:` line fix the spec and rerun once. 5. List it under `Added` as `queued update: <id> (<fields>)`; skip finish: the skill drains. Reply block keeps its ten field names: Operation adds `update`; Result for sync, add and update is the first queued line; Added names `queued update: <id> (<fields>)` for update; 'Sync, add and update run no check'. Stop conditions: an update id the script refuses (retired, split, unknown) is relayed verbatim.

decisions.question: How does a split that finds the catalog lease held wait for it, once the lease moves to just before its dry run (catalog_lock waits 10 s by default)?

options.summary: lease acquire --wait SECONDS in the driver; the split passes --wait 300 and reruns acquire up to 3 times in all on a held-lease refusal; the default stays 10 s
No driver change; the agent prose loops on the 10 s acquire
acquire waits until the 30-minute lease staleness

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17. The project rule puts settings a driver can act on in the driver, not in prose; 300 s plus the run fits one Bash call under its 600 s cap.

decisions.question: Where do queued field updates live and what drains them?

options.summary: The same todo-inbox folder and name scheme, files holding {"updates": [...]}; add --inbox drains adds and updates oldest first in one write; the todo-watch mod is unchanged
A sibling update --inbox drain with its own folder or name prefix; the mod gains a second drain call

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17. One drain keeps one catalog write and one summary line; the mod drains by running add --inbox and passes its inbox: line through unparsed.

decisions.question: Which item fields may a queued update set?

options.summary: Exactly the fields an add spec may carry, less issue and url

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17. The add spec list is already validated (types and the item schema); links, sources, issues, tracker and computed fields stay with the script.

decisions.question: What skill surface comes with the driver changes?

options.summary: todo-edit --split takes several ids and --update ID[, ID ...] -- <guidance> is new; either dispatches one todo-editor per id in one message; --update drains once
Multi-id --split only; updates are queued by any agent with inbox put --update, documented only

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17. Issue 309 acceptance dispatches three splits in one message; the update operation gives research findings a queued route into the catalog.
